title: Land post-e0d Beads planning export on the integration line
description: poc-16-eng intentionally integrated the chained-auth code through e0d9f4d. After that landing, reconcile the newer committed .beads/issues.jsonl planning from codex/poc-16-chained-auth into the integration line. This includes the poc-16-x1o epic and all children, poc-16-yez.14, the corrected poc-16-t9f confidentiality-boundary wording, the purge-triggered recipient-generation refinements, and their dependency edges. Preserve concurrent integration-branch graph changes; do not replace the full export blindly or drop either graph.
acceptance_criteria: The integration branch's committed issues.jsonl contains every poc-16-x1o child and dependency, poc-16-yez.14, and the corrected poc-16-t9f design text; all references resolve, IDs are unique, bd dep cycles reports none, and a deterministic bd export matches the reconciled file. The reconciliation is committed before poc-16-t53 lands the integration line on main.

title: Review encryption-key supersession and retirement against T_supp
description: Review the new encryption lifecycle as a revocation/suppression boundary before rotation integration. Decide whether recipient-key supersession, old root/HistoryNode key_wrap retirement, content-frontier retirement, removed-device exclusion, and purge-complete evidence belong in the global suppression/death-key match tree or remain explicit causal predecessor/retirement refs plus local erasure state. Check backward/out-of-range and future matches, successor forks, replayed root and cover wraps, removed recipients, and the rule that suppression changes projection/closure but never rewrites stable validity. Resolve the compositional case where a first F purge rotates once, key healing later wraps survivor cover nodes to the successor generation, and a later purge must rotate again if it retires one of those nodes. Ensure no design treats hiding a ciphertext row as proof that private key material was destroyed. This bead is review/planning only; implementation stays in poc-16-x1o.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an arrival-order-independent matrix for recipient public facts, local recipient private material, root and HistoryNode key_wrap facts, content frontiers, removed devices, past ciphertext, and future ciphertext. For each transition, identify stable validation, explicit refs/needs, T_supp extraction/resolve_supp, projection hiding, local purge, recipient-generation trigger, and publication boundary. Resolve whether any new death/supp keys or closure edges are required; add implementation beads rather than implementing them here. The result must leave timestamps causally inert and must block archived root/cover-wrap resurrection after recipient supersession.

title: Benchmark cover growth, enclave handles, rotation, and rewrap fanout
description: Measure the operational cost of the chosen design under realistic and adversarial histories: dense/sparse authoring, random and clustered punctures, many workspaces, many devices, many live frontiers, offline recipients, recipient rotation, healing, and large files. Separate local KDF/cover work, hardware operations, durable ciphertext growth, T_fact/T_supp overhead, network wrap fanout, and restart/recovery time.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmarks report p50/p95/p99 and storage/handle counts across documented sizes. Results demonstrate hardware handles scale with active workspace/recipient generations rather than content count and compare cover growth with the theoretical tree bound. Measure recipient rotation separately for first-F root loss and later retirement of wrapped/healed cover nodes, including migration and O(live-frontier/device/cover) rewrap healing; report worst-case rotation cadence rather than assuming once per F. Thresholds and failure behavior for hardware handle exhaustion are documented and enforced by regression guards where stable.

title: Document migration, guarantees, operations, and release gates
description: Update DESIGN.md/WORKSPACES.md and operator/user documentation to replace stable dev_box content wrapping with the selected rotating recipient design, describe the KDF/cover/puncture graph, distinguish content-frontier versus recipient rotation, and explain suppression visibility versus purge completion. Plan versioned migration for existing plaintext content/keychain state, interrupted upgrades, mixed-version peers, provider capability changes, backups, device loss, and recovery. Include the accepted revocation/T_supp review and source lineage.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh-workspace walkthrough and an upgrade fixture both pass the complete test suite. Migration is restartable, never writes plaintext into synced facts, and either finishes on the new version or fails closed with recoverable old state. Documentation states exactly what `purge complete` guarantees on each provider tier, how offline peers affect eventual forward secrecy, why timestamps do not encode causality, and which explicit refs/closure edges do. Release gates name the adversarial and scale suites and require no unresolved P0/P1 security findings.

title: Drive confidentiality purge from global suppression closure
description: Connect validated poc-16 suppression to encryption without putting suppression into stable fact validity. When resolve_supp/T_supp surfaces a valid deletion and its victims through pile closure, enqueue explicit coordinate-based puncture work after the suppression root/manifest publication boundary. Handle victim-before-deletion, deletion-before-victim, out-of-range discovery, future victims, duplicate sync, and restart. Projection disappearance and cryptographic purge are distinct states: UI may hide promptly, but only the local rotation/purge state machine can claim confidentiality completion.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests on multiple peers cover both arrival orders, out-of-range T_supp discovery, future matching facts, concurrent manifest readers, failure before/after suppression-root CAS, restart, duplicate delivery, and offline convergence. Stable validity is byte-identical before/after suppression; the closed pile contains the causal deletion evidence; no SQL/global lookup is used to decide validity; and purge is launched exactly once per explicit victim operation while safely resuming duplicates.

title: Integrate membership removal, frontier rotation, rewrap, and key healing
description: Keep membership removal's content-frontier rotation separate from puncture-triggered recipient rotation. An authorized removal fact causally refs the membership/frontier it changes; a new monotonically linked content frontier generates fresh F and wraps only to remaining active recipient successor facts. If recipient rotation invalidates predecessor wraps, normal key request/healing rewraps every still-live frontier to the successor: F only while F remains live, otherwise the canonical retained HistoryNode cover with exact coordinates/tombstone context—never a retired F or deleted leaf. Serving a healing wrap makes that cover node recovery-bound to the recipient generation, so a later purge of it triggers another rotation. Specify offline peers, simultaneous removal/purge, recipient successor forks, and recovery when a device has only part of the retained cover.
acceptance_criteria: Three-or-more-peer tests remove a device, rotate the content frontier, continue authoring, and prove the removed device cannot open new content. Independent tests rotate one remaining recipient due to F purge and heal unrelated live frontiers/root-or-cover material to its successor. A new device joining a punctured frontier receives only the canonical survivor cover, opens survivors, and cannot open deleted content; purging a healed cover node advances its recipient generation. Out-of-order removal/frontier/recipient/wrap facts converge through refs and closure, never timestamp ordering. Requests for retired F, retired recipients, removed devices, or deleted coordinates fail.

title: Audit all secret copies and add adversarial forward-secrecy tests
description: Threat-model and test every place F, leaf, cover, recipient private material, decrypted plaintext, and archived wraps can survive: Python/Rust objects, caches, queues, SQLite tables/WAL/journals, temp files, blobs, crash dumps/logging, backup/export, treap piles, manifests, delivery logs, and enclave sealed state. Exercise post-purge compromise, stale snapshot, malicious re-delivery, peer lag, and interrupted rotation. File separate beads for revocation/suppression issues discovered; do not fold unrelated revocation fixes into this implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A storage-surface inventory links each secret to an owner and purge hook. Automated adversarial tests retain ciphertext plus old root/history-node wraps, complete an initial F purge and at least one later healed-cover purge, then attempt every supported recovery path and fail for the claimed tier while still opening survivor content. Memory/cache test hooks verify eviction and best-effort zeroization. Backup/export/log fixtures contain no plaintext or local private material. Any untestable platform guarantee is explicitly scoped and documented, not asserted.

title: Rotate recipient eph generations on wrap-bound key purge
description: Implement recipient rotation as a resumable local state machine driven by the puncture worker's explicit retirement set. A purge transition advances the recipient generation exactly once when it retires any secret recoverable through the current generation: F, a wrapped retained HistoryNode, or a locally generation-sealed equivalent. The original poc-10 first-F-wipe rule remains the root-only special case; later punctures skip rotation only when none of their retired nodes is wrap/generation-bound. Prepare a fresh recipient ephemeral keypair and one self-signed successor fact naming the old recipient; migrate surviving KDF cover plus other still-live local roots/cover records; retire every old-generation wrap; destroy the old private handle and canonical/local copies; then mark purge complete. Because database and secure-hardware deletion are not one transaction, persist monotonic phases and never expose a false completed guarantee. Preserve the prepared successor/timestamp across retries instead of generating it from lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Crash injection at every phase (before/after new-key generation, successor persistence, each cover/root migration batch, DB commit, old-wrap purge, hardware-key destroy, and completion marker) converges without reverting phase, generating multiple successors, losing surviving content, or claiming completion while old material works. An F-only frontier rotates on its first F wipe and not on later unwrapped-cover punctures; if healing wraps a survivor cover node to the current recipient, later purging that node rotates again and its archived wrap cannot recover it. A batch retiring multiple bound nodes rotates once. Concurrent purges serialize/merge against an explicit generation predecessor without timestamp arbitration. Strong-tier rollback tests reject restored pre-purge sealed snapshots.

title: Implement bounded local secret provider and encrypted cover store
description: Implement the key-provider boundary selected by the hardware ADR: generate/use/destroy recipient ephemeral private handles; envelope-seal F and retained-cover nodes to the active generation; enumerate/migrate live ciphertext records without exporting a hardware private key; and report provider capabilities. Keep stable identity/attestation operations separate from content unwrapping. The software test provider must model deletion and rollback honestly rather than pretending filesystem deletion is a Secure Enclave guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests run against an in-memory fault provider and every available real/software provider. They cover handle deletion, wrong generation/AAD, partial migration, locked/unavailable hardware, restart, backup restore, zeroization of transient buffers where the language permits it, and provider capability reporting. Stress tests store many cover nodes while keeping hardware handles bounded by active workspace/recipient generations. No retained stable root API can request or derive a retired generation.

title: Encrypt messages and files with KDF leaf keys
description: Replace plaintext message and file fact payloads with versioned AEAD ciphertext using the KDF leaf selected by the explicit content coordinate and frontier ref. Authenticate all clear routing/authorization/dependency fields as AAD. Define whether file descriptors and chunks use distinct derived subkeys/nonces, and preserve sealed-but-not-yet-openable projection so ciphertext may sync before the recipient has cover material. Keep plaintext out of durable fact bytes, treap piles, manifests, delivery logs, blob filenames/metadata, and ordinary projection rows.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic multi-peer tests author, sync, open, restart, and late-deliver messages plus small/large files; ciphertext-before-wrap later opens through dependency/key healing. Tampering with ciphertext, nonce, coordinate, frontier, channel, parent, signer, chunk index, or size fails closed. Raw scans of fact/blob/index/app databases, WAL/journal files, manifests, logs, and sync payloads find no test plaintext. Same prepared authoring input retries without consulting latest state.

title: Implement exact/range puncture and durable secret erasure
description: Port poc-10's exact leaf retirement and time-prefix/range chop. Given an explicit validated victim coordinate/range and content frontier, materialize survivor siblings, atomically replace the old cover with the canonical new cover, exact-delete the leaf/descend path/F when applicable, purge canonical secret bytes and transient caches, and retain only non-secret tombstone/retirement evidence needed to prevent resurrection. Emit an explicit retirement set identifying every removed F/history/leaf secret plus whether it has any shared wrap, local generation-sealed copy, or other recovery edge under the current recipient generation. Rotation consumes that explicit set; neither retry state nor wrap-bound status is inferred from timestamps or latest-row lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests puncture random leaves/ranges in varying orders and compare decryptability with an oracle. The victim cannot be derived from any retained node while every live coordinate remains openable. Duplicate/reordered purge work is idempotent from its explicit operation id/basis refs. Fault tests cover the local database transaction and canonical-byte/WAL cleanup. The first transition that removes F reports F and its recovery edges; later transitions accurately report retired cover nodes. Tests distinguish an unwrapped retired node (no rotation trigger) from the same node with an archived/shared wrap or current-generation sealed copy (rotation trigger).

title: Implement canonical retained-cover and lazy leaf derivation
description: Represent the decryptable remainder after punctures as the canonical prefix-free sibling cover from poc-10. Derive fresh leaves from F or the deepest retained covering sibling, materialize only what authoring/opening or a puncture needs, and reject a coordinate with no retained ancestor. Persist secret-bearing cover nodes only through the selected encrypted local-secret provider; public graph/pile state may carry coordinates and tombstones but never node secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Model/property tests compare randomized author/puncture/open sequences with a simple set-of-live-leaves oracle, prove the cover is prefix-free/non-overlapping and cannot cover a punctured coordinate, and show all surviving coordinates still derive the expected leaf. Restart tests reconstruct the same cover. Measurements demonstrate no one-key-per-content durable state: fresh operation stays near one root plus lazily used leaves, and p punctures grow with the tree cover bound rather than total content count.

title: Add content frontiers, recipient successors, and bound key_wrap facts
description: Port poc-10's removal_frontier/local_key_secret, workspace-scoped local_recipient_key/recipient_key, and key_wrap design using poc-16 facts and closure. Initial and replacement content_frontier facts use explicit predecessor/authority refs and bind the selected workspace-or-channel scope; random F is local secret material, never shared plaintext. The local recipient private half is generated independently and stored through the selected hardware provider; the shared public fact is self-signed by stable device identity. Rotation publishes one successor recipient fact that explicitly refs/names the predecessor and simultaneously retires it; active/fork behavior is graph-defined and arrival-order-independent, never latest-timestamp selection. A key_wrap binds workspace/channel scope, frontier, recipient fact id, algorithm/version, WrappedSecretKind (FrontierRoot or HistoryNode), exact node coordinate/source/tombstone context, sender authorization, and ciphertext as AEAD associated data.
acceptance_criteria: Real X25519+AEAD tests cover initial F creation/distribution, root and retained HistoryNode wraps, two peers, multiple frontiers per recipient, wrong scope/frontier/secret-kind/node-coordinate/recipient/AAD, replay, tamper, predecessor from another device, successor-before-predecessor, duplicate delivery, retry, and concurrent successor attempts. After successor closure, new wraps never target the predecessor. A retired root/leaf cannot be mislabeled and rewrapped as a live HistoryNode. Shared facts contain public/ciphertext material only; local F and recipient private bytes never enter T_fact, T_supp, piles, manifests, delivery logs, app projections, or sync.

title: Specify explicit content coordinates and causal encryption refs
description: Define the shared and local fact shapes after the workspace-vs-channel content-key granularity decision is recorded. A shared content fact carries an explicit fresh 256-bit content coordinate (or an equivalently collision-resistant prepared authoring nonce), its scoped content-frontier ref, authorization refs, and ciphertext. The timestamp is captured as now on first authoring and may select the time-tree bucket only. Retry reuses the same prepared inputs; it never queries the latest timestamp/key/frontier to manufacture determinism. Derived local KDF/retirement artifacts carry no timestamp or copy the basis fact's timestamp as inert metadata. content_frontier and recipient_key successor facts explicitly name predecessors; key_wrap names recipient, frontier, wrapped-secret kind, and exact root/history-node coordinate; suppression/deletion names its victim/death key so closure, not temporal comparison, relates facts.
acceptance_criteria: A schema/closure diagram and codecs pin every ref, need, signed field, coordinate, and AEAD-associated-data field. Tests prove two facts from the same author with the same timestamp get distinct leaves; retrying a saved prepared command is byte-identical without a database read or clock call; out-of-order arrival converges by dependency closure; and changing timestamp alone cannot grant authority, select an active recipient, supersede a key, or satisfy a causal need.

title: Decide secure-hardware key hierarchy and purge guarantee tiers
description: Choose how poc-16 protects a potentially large retained KDF cover without creating one Secure Enclave/KeyStore handle per content key. Separate stable device signing/attestation identity from rotating content-unwrapping state. Compare independently generated non-exportable recipient ephemeral keys, a forward-only generation ratchet, and a permanent enclave root guarded by rollback-resistant monotonic state. Reject any design in which a stable dev_box/root can derive an old generation or reopen an archived F wrap. Define how cover-node ciphertexts are envelope-encrypted under the active generation, when survivor material migrates, what is destroyed, how handle quotas are bounded, and which guarantees are possible on Apple/Android/TPM/software-only providers.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR selects the primary hierarchy and a portable fallback, with key/handle counts, backup/restore behavior, enclave API assumptions, crash windows, and explicit normal-disk vs hardware-backed vs rollback-resistant guarantee tiers. A restored old sealed-state snapshot cannot recover retired keys in any tier claiming rollback resistance. The ADR includes a concrete rotate→migrate→destroy protocol and rejects deterministic old-key derivation from a retained root unless hardware monotonic state makes old generations permanently inaccessible.

title: Port the two-axis KDF core with cross-implementation vectors
description: Implement a small pure/executable core for F → power-of-two time-range splits → within-bucket 256-bit content-coordinate trie, preserving poc-10's domain separation (`topo time split v1`, `topo trie split v1`) unless the source-contract bead versions a change. Time is only an address into the first axis; the fresh content coordinate supplies uniqueness on the second. Make child derivation, coverage checks, coordinate encoding, and AEAD leaf-key derivation explicit and usable by running encryption/puncture code.
acceptance_criteria: Known-answer tests consume the frozen poc-10/poc-16 fixtures and cover root boundaries, left/right splits, minute/bucket edges, 256 trie bits, invalid geometry, domain separation, and distinct same-timestamp content coordinates. Property tests show a child is deterministic from explicit inputs and no API reads a clock or database. Runtime content encryption calls this verified/tested core rather than a parallel model.

title: Freeze poc-10 encryption lineage, threat model, and test vectors
description: Turn the relevant poc-10 lineage into the port's explicit source contract: 7f60936f/ad380cb4 (two-axis per-content puncturing), 536b13c3/9b40f352/bdaa60f6 (derive, wipe, and retained-sibling recovery), 178f198b→341b8c37→ed04d84f/122cc471 (wrap-bound root-loss recipient rotation and purge), and the later key-healing design that wraps retained HistoryNode secrets when F is gone. Resolve the historical wording conflict in favor of the implemented root-loss rule, then document the required composition: the original first-F-wipe/once-per-F result assumes no later retired secret remains recoverable through that recipient generation; once a retained cover node is wrapped or generation-sealed, purging that node is another key-purge trigger and must advance the recipient generation. Record the post-purge disk/snapshot attacker, availability tradeoffs, and the narrower contribution from poc-13's connection ephemeral_secret/close/test_close_purge design (suppression verdict immediately purges secret-bearing facts, but no separate content-recipient rotation). Identify every intentional poc-16 deviation before implementation, especially explicit causal refs and content coordinates.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in design record maps each poc-10 source type/transition to its poc-16 counterpart, cites the source commits, and contains a state/secret ownership table plus an adversary matrix. Versioned fixtures cover F generation, both KDF domains, left/right splits, leaf derivation, root and HistoryNode wrap/open, a first-F-wipe trace, and a later wrapped-cover-node purge trace. The record states that key purge—not deletion timestamp—is the recipient-rotation trigger and that timestamps are now-only metadata/addresses, never causality, authorization, supersession, or retry ordering.

title: Puncturable content encryption + KDF history tree (poc-10 port)
description: Port poc-10 content encryption into poc-16: a random secret F per content frontier; a domain-separated two-axis KDF (time bucket as an address only, then a 256-bit content-coordinate trie); lazy leaf derivation; a canonical retained-sibling cover; exact/range puncture; encrypted content facts; and wrap-based recovery. Preserve poc-10's refined root-loss rule as a special case and close its composition with history-node healing: on each peer, a local key purge that retires any secret recoverable through the current recipient generation—F, a wrapped retained cover node, or a locally generation-sealed equivalent—triggers one eager recipient ephemeral-key rotation for that purge transition. When F is the only wrapped covering secret, this reduces to poc-10's rule that the first actual F wipe rotates once and later punctures do not; if healing later wraps cover nodes, purging one of those nodes rotates again so an archived wrap cannot resurrect it. One self-signed successor recipient fact names the predecessor, future wraps target the successor, surviving cover/root material migrates monotonically, and the old private key plus old wraps/canonical copies are destroyed before purge completion. Keep content-frontier rotation for membership removal distinct from purge-triggered recipient rotation. A long-lived device signing/attestation key may survive, but no stable dev_box, enclave root operation, deterministic derivation path, archived wrap, or rollbackable sealed snapshot may remain able to reconstruct a retired F, cover node, or leaf. Large retained covers are encrypted as data under bounded active recipient generations, not represented by one enclave key handle per content item. If a permanent hardware root is retained, it may authenticate or unwrap only the live generation and must enforce non-rollbackable monotonic retirement; otherwise the implementation must use independently generated deletable keys and state a weaker snapshot guarantee. Timestamps are authored as now and have zero causal, authorization, supersession, or retry-ordering weight; explicit refs, needs, and pile closure establish relationships. Derived local artifacts either carry no timestamp or copy their basis fact's timestamp solely as deterministic metadata. Compose confidentiality retirement with the global suppression match tree without making suppression part of stable validity.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed. Cross-implementation vectors pin the poc-10 KDF geometry and intentional poc-16 coordinate/rotation deviations. Realistic multi-peer tests prove surviving content remains decryptable while a suppressed leaf, retired F or cover node, archived old key_wrap, superseded recipient private key, plaintext cache/WAL copy, and—on the strong hardware tier—a restored pre-purge sealed-state snapshot cannot recover deleted plaintext after purge completion. Fault injection at every migration/rotation phase proves retries resume monotonically, never mint a timestamp or causal edge from a latest-row lookup, rotate exactly once for each purge transition that retires material recoverable by the current generation, skip rotation when no retired secret is wrap/generation-bound, and never publish a false purge-complete state. Scale results bound enclave handles by active workspaces/generations rather than content count, show retained secret state grows with the canonical cover rather than one key per fact, and measure recipient fanout, history-node healing, purge-triggered rotation, and rewrap costs. Documentation distinguishes ordinary storage deletion, hardware-backed deletion, and rollback-resistant cryptographic erasure.

title: Land the integration line on main
description: main is docs-only: every closed 808/jbg/yez/zgj implementation bead lives on codex/all-night-20260724, and the auth tail on codex/poc-16-chained-auth. Merge the integration line onto main after poc-16-eng lands the tail, and keep main the branch of record from then on.

title: Land chained-auth tail into the integration line
description: Integrate codex/poc-16-chained-auth at e0d9f4d from /home/holmes/poc-16-chained-auth. Preserve the seven post-d73f627 commits covering stable mint/retry state, convergent mint proofs, idempotent pile retries, pre-manifest recovery, failed-turn rollback, and their regressions. Reconcile overlaps with the tree/kernel/mint/pump simplification already on codex/all-night-20260724; do not silently drop behavior from either line.
acceptance_criteria: The semantic changes in d73f627..e0d9f4d are present on the integration branch; overlapping runtime/projection behavior is reconciled with 808.5; focused auth/projection restart tests and the full suite pass; own-agent and Fable reviews are satisfied or Fable unavailability is recorded per the session instruction; the source worktree remains intact unless separately authorized.
notes: Order immediately after active bead poc-16-808.5 and before poc-16-808.6, because both lines touch node projection/crash boundaries and resolving them once minimizes conflict.
close_reason: Merged chained-auth tail semantics with the simplification runtime; canonical mint, crash/restart rollback, sync invalidation, and projection-log ordering regressions pass. Own-agent and Claude Fable reviews approved; full suite 157 passed, 10 planned skips.

title: Verify suppression is invisible before manifest publication
description: The current derived removal global can become visible to mint after a failed turn dirties SQLite but before the manifest CAS. The generic projection recovery work in poc-16-zgj.20 restores today's publication boundary; when the global suppression match tree is implemented, explicitly re-audit that no new suppression affects authorization until its manifest generation commits.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection before suppression-tree manifest CAS proves the old root remains authoritative to mint; same-process retry publishes the suppression once; restart, app/index rebuild, and concurrent-reader cases preserve the same boundary.

title: Restore authoritative projections before failed turns escape
description: A turn that fails after merge() dirties the derived index but before manifest publication currently returns control to the live daemon with uncommitted-to-root facts/globals still observable. This can change mint authorization until another turn or restart rebuilds. Repair the derived index and app projection from the authoritative root on the failure path before releasing the workspace lock, while retaining ingress for retry.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection before manifest CAS proves the manifest remains authoritative, an uncommitted membership/removal cannot affect mint evaluation after the failed call returns, the ingress pile remains, and a same-process retry admits the change exactly once.
close_reason: Failed-turn regression now faults the real manifest CAS during a signed removal and proves the old root still authorizes mint, global/app changes remain absent, transactions close, ingress stays retained, and same-process retry publishes once; full 88-test suite passes.

title: Recover index-ahead state after a pre-CAS crash
description: merge() commits new facts into the derived index before commit() publishes the manifest. If execution fails in that window, the old index generation stamp still appears current; retry sees no new ids, skips projection, publishes the fact, and stamps an incomplete app model. Mark the index generation dirty transactionally with index mutation and rebuild from the authoritative root before retry.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic fault immediately after merge and before manifest commit leaves the pile recoverable; restart/retry rebuilds the dirty index from the old root, then admits and projects the fact exactly once; index and app generation stamps match the resulting root; full suite and benchmark guards pass.
close_reason: Index root stamps are invalidated transactionally with merge/rebuild mutations and restored only after manifest publication; pre-CAS restart/replay regression, 84-test suite, and all 5k guards pass.

title: Make device projection replay and crash idempotent
description: The changed-fid roster optimization still materializes replayed device claims before filtering reconciliation. A stale lower-fid/rank-losing claim can overwrite the canonical projection, and a crash after root/index commit but before app materialization leaves the same inconsistency on retry. Make the read model generation-aware or otherwise ensure replays are canonical/no-op.
acceptance_criteria: A stale losing device claim cannot replace the canonical roster row; retry after commit-before-materialize repairs the app projection; ordinary device-authored writes still avoid a full roster rebuild; realistic regression tests cover both failure modes.
close_reason: App projections now carry a manifest-generation stamp, lagging projections rebuild before replay, and aligned replays materialize only new ids; crash and stale-loser regressions pass.

title: Make FsStore concurrent puts atomic
description: The chained-auth black-box suite exposed concurrent PUTs to the same FsStore key sharing p+'.tmp'. One thread renames that pathname and the other raises FileNotFoundError, returning HTTP 500. Use per-write unique temp files while preserving atomic os.replace and clean abandoned temps.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic concurrent-put regression makes both writers complete without error, leaves one complete value at the key, and leaves no temp files; the full suite passes.
close_reason: FsStore now uses unique same-directory temp files for atomic concurrent puts; deterministic race regression and black-box test pass; Codex and Claude Fable approved.

title: Reschedule sync after quarantine restoration
description: A walk can restore a locally quarantined fact only after its push set was computed, then cache the peer ETag against the new local root. Later 304 responses may return early forever, so the restored fact never reaches the peer and roots remain divergent.
acceptance_criteria: Restoring any quarantined fact invalidates or reschedules every peer walk cache for that workspace; add a realistic two-peer regression that restores after push-set calculation and proves a subsequent no-new-write walk converges; retain ordinary 304 pruning when no restoration occurs.
close_reason: Quarantine restoration now invalidates every workspace peer cache so the next unchanged walk republishes restored facts; realistic two-peer pull-then-follow-up-push regression passes.

title: Bind mint evaluation to committed canonical authority
description: A caller can present an independently valid stale closure that omits a committed conflicting authority winner. Evaluate mode currently canonicalizes only inside the caller-controlled pile, so a fact pruned from the workspace canonical set can still authorize a sync token.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate mode compares presented need providers with committed canonical providers while preserving globals-blind durable validation and first-sync for genuinely new descendants; add a regression for a quarantined losing device chain and a positive fresh-delegation case; pass the canonical workspace view atomically from the mint seam.
close_reason: Committed canonical evaluation now checks semantic need compatibility, not provider-id equality: incompatible co-offer winners reject stale quarantined chains while honest diverged peers mint both ways and can converge.

title: Hoisting in production: settle-node closure placement (ρ→1); retire flat per-leaf closure
description: SIMPLIFY.md §2 ('optional settle hook = hoisting', hoist.py's _spans/_settle) + MULTILEVEL_PILE.md. Land hoisting in the PRODUCTION store/sync path as an engine capability on tree.py (808.2): factor each closure fact ONCE to its settle node (the LCA of the leaves needing it), so every root-to-node path is a closed set and full-sync download drops to one copy of each fact — ρ→1 vs the flat per-leaf-closure ρ≈3x measured. Replaces layout.py's per-leaf close(). Keep the two identities distinct: fp (in-range keys, the diff identity) vs oid (h(pile bytes), closure included, the fetch identity) — so hoisted closure copies stay out of the diff algebra. Range-sync becomes a flat shared-core tax (MULTILEVEL_PILE A.4-A.5; key order must be dep-aligned or it can lose to leaf-only piles for small pulls). Verify against the prototype measurements (bench_hoist, bench_hoist_sync, bench_order). SHARED-POOL BENEFIT: T_supp (yez.2/yez.10) reuses the SAME content-addressed settle-node closure pool as T_fact — one hoisted closure store across both trees. Status today: hoist.py is PROTOTYPE/bench-only (not in node/walk/kernel); this bead is its production landing, distinct from 808.3 which only deletes hoist._judge on the kernel side.

title: Make removal projection independent of membership materialization order
description: A valid removal can have an older timestamp than the target's membership fact. During canonical reprojection, close() may materialize the removal before the user row; removal's UPDATE then affects zero rows and the later user materialization inserts evicted=0. The same accepted fact set can therefore expose a non-evicted member after rebuild/reprojection even though the removal global is present. Resolve this with the suppression/remove-wins model rather than relying on projector order.
acceptance_criteria: Add a regression with an old-timestamp removal preceding target membership during reprojection; prove fresh projection, rebuild, and opposite arrival orders expose the same removed state; preserve stable validation and parallel drain; implement remove-wins through the global suppression design or another explicitly approved order-independent projection rule.

title: Property suite: E order-independence + rebuild equivalence (fold± ≡ fold over E)

(b) THE theorem: live fold-with-retractions over delivery order == clean fold over E in canonical order (rebuild computes S first from T_supp/root, zero retractions fire). (c) Contract extensions: deletion refs its target; suppression facts not themselves suppressible (S stays monotone); pump-twice = no change; pump crash/resume.
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: tests/test_eset.py (E order-independence, monotone S, verdicts never read S) + THE-theorem section of tests/test_pump.py (fold± over D == fold over E; rebuild fires zero retractions).

title: Suppression closure edge in the kernel (resolve_supp), validity-independent
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3/§3a. Give the kernel a suppression closure edge: for a fact with a suppression key, resolve the head of its K-group in T_supp; a deletion marker there means the deletion is part of that fact's closure and rides along. This is 'the kernel has to check the tree to know the closure' — but as a CLOSURE edge, NOT a validity input: the fact stays valid, only flagged suppressed, so validity stays globals-blind and parallel drain stays safe. Mirrors resolve_deps. Concurrency needs NO write-time match: T_supp is a CvRDT, concurrent deletion+target writes converge (two-root merge = set union); the only cost is latency-to-visibility (self-healing staleness), not a data race.
notes: Q1/Q3: resolve_supp is a mask-after-judgment closure edge; it fires at MERGE and SERVE (per suppression-participant), NOT at projection. It WRITES the discovery as a ±fid delivery-log row (SIMPLIFY §5 log(seq,±fid)); the pump/projection folds the log with ZERO tree walking. S never lives in app.db (lives in T_supp/root). Cost O(S·log N) at ingest, monotone, paid once.

acceptance_criteria: Produce an explicit matrix for direct user authorship, bearer descendants, device descendants, delegated admins, relayed facts, past facts, and future facts; map each verdict to stable validation, suppression closure/projection, or the mint/transport gate; identify required deathkey/suppkey extraction and closure dependencies; update the plan of record and unblock poc-16-gxz with a testable implementation boundary.

Preserve the current branch's stable-validation/history-independence constraints; investigate and choose the enforcement seam rather than patching it opportunistically.
acceptance_criteria: Add a realistic regression that demonstrates relay by a distinct active member; specify direct authorship and delegated user/device/admin behavior after removal; reject post-removal authority at a protocol seam that remains arrival-order-independent and convergent; cover the chosen behavior in black-box multi-peer tests and document the token/drain threat model.

(1) closure_sync(Q) on T_fact yields D but MISSES out-of-range victims (surface the bug). (2) supp_walk(T_supp, prefix=chan=X) surfaces them. Assert: (a) surfaced==true chan=X set (ground truth from seed); (b) treap node fetches only — instrumented counting store, ZERO idx/SQL calls, fetch count O(matches+depth) not O(M); (c) project(closure) suppresses every chan=X fact in- and out-of-range; (d) shuffled build ⇒ byte-identical T_supp root. Mirrors bench/bench_sync.py + hoist prototype.

title: Surfacing pass close_deletions: one-sided RBSR range walk per death key

Cost O(matches+depth), not O(set). Returns a deletion-closed set.
notes: REFINED: resolved as a CLOSURE EDGE at three call sites (sync/kernel/projection), not a one-off pass. Two directions: target->deletion = single head-of-group leaf check (N:1, projection-critical); deletion->targets = range scan (1:N, the out-of-range proof). See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.

Keeps persistent-validity globals-blind (suppression = projection-time verdict, never a validation input); project must never surface a now-suppressed fact. No globals CAS on the persistent path.

Second content-addressed Merkle treap over the SAME fact set, key = suppkey||ts:fid, so all facts sharing a death key sort contiguously (the deletion + its N victims). Pure function of the set; built/maintained by the EXISTING treap.build/treap.update (blind incremental = the 'update the tree on new suppression keys' requirement). Facts with no suppression attribute are absent.
notes:
REFINED (concurrency turn): T_supp is a SYNCED tree (second root per ws), NOT locally derived — syncing the index is how out-of-range facts surface. Tag-ordered key: suppkey||tag||ts:fid, deletions tag=0 (sort to group head), targets tag=1. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.
Q4/Q5 (2026-07-24): T_supp leaves are CLOSED piles — each deletion rides with its OWN validity closure (admin/authority chain, signatures); only valid deletions enter S (S(D)=targets of *valid* suppression facts). That closure is SHARED (one admin deletes many channels) so ρ≈3x leaf-dup hits T_supp too — production T_supp must ride the HOISTING engine (808.2 tree.py / jbg.1 fat nodes), NOT the flat per-leaf-close prototype, and shares ONE content-addressed hoisted closure pool with T_fact (only index nodes extra, ~x2). The yez.6 proof may use the prototype; production must not. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3b + SIMPLIFY.md §3.

title: Flatten repository into docs/, core/, and facts/
description: Perform a behavior-preserving repository reorganization. Move every project documentation file except root AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, and README.md into docs/ and repair all cross-references. Replace the tinyp2p/ namespace with root core/ and facts/ packages: move the non-facts modules currently directly under tinyp2p/ into core/, and promote tinyp2p/facts/** to facts/**. Update imports, package metadata, tests, benches, scripts, daemon entry points, and documentation references; remove stale paths and avoid compatibility shims unless a documented external API requires one.
acceptance_criteria: No tracked project documentation remains at the root except AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, and README.md; tinyp2p/ is gone; core/ owns the former tinyp2p core/runtime modules and facts/ owns the former tinyp2p/facts families; rg finds no stale tinyp2p imports or obsolete doc paths except intentional migration notes; packaging/import smoke tests, full pytest, relevant bench entry-point smoke tests, and docs links pass; the change is predominantly mechanical and preserves behavior.
notes: Schedule after poc-16-808.8 so documentation is folded back before paths move, and before deployment packaging where possible. Keep this as one reviewed rename commit plus only the minimal import/reference fixes needed for green tests.

title: Make index generation stamping exception-safe
description: An exception partway through _stamp() can leave an implicit SQLite transaction open with a visible uncommitted root row. _sync_index then mistakes it for alignment and the next merge fails BEGIN with a nested-transaction error. Roll back partial stamp writes and make same-process recovery converge.
acceptance_criteria: A fault between root and version stamp writes leaves no open transaction; the retained pile retries in the same process and index/app stamps converge to the published root.
close_reason: Index generation stamping now rolls back partial writes; trigger-backed atomicity and mid-stamp same-process retry regressions pass.

title: Keep changed-fid projection filtering linear
description: Device reconciliation tests membership in merge's changed-fid list for every closure-expanded valid, making bulk ingest O(U*V). Normalize changed IDs to a set once at the projection boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Changed-fid filtering uses set-like membership and a realistic bulk regression demonstrates it does not perform list membership per valid.
close_reason: Projection boundary normalizes changed ids to a frozenset once; bulk closure-replay regression rejects linear list membership.

title: Avoid replay-driven full device roster projection
description: Reviewed closure piles replay already-known device facts on every device-authored write. device.reconcile sees those replayed device_key offers and deletes/reinserts the full workspace device roster even though no canonical winner changed, making ordinary writes O(total devices).
acceptance_criteria: Materialize/reconcile only newly admitted facts unless canonical pruning/restoration requires a full reprojection; add a realistic device-authored ordinary-write regression proving the roster is not rebuilt; preserve winner-switch reprojection and pass the full suite.
close_reason: Device reconciliation now considers only newly admitted facts during ordinary turns and uses the full active set only for canonical reprojection; device-authored writes no longer rebuild the roster and winner-switch tests remain green.

title: Keep direct device grants deterministic across proof-winner changes
description: A direct grant that inherits its current canonical device provider's timestamp changes fid if an equal-valid provider later becomes canonical. A retry then misses the exact fact and fails as already enrolled, violating deterministic lost-response and reconcile retries.
acceptance_criteria: Derive the mandatory Fact timestamp from immutable workspace/logical-cell input without scanning for an existing logical grant; preserve the rule that timestamps carry no causal weight; add a restart retry and a canonical-provider-switch retry regression.
close_reason: Direct grants derive their required timestamp from the immutable workspace anchor, never a mutable proof winner or logical-cell scan; restart and provider-switch retry regressions pass.

title: Opt-in authoritative suppression read mode (DO/CAS); default stays eventual
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3a/§6. Default suppression is fast-eventual (walk T_supp; a to-be-suppressed fact may briefly project live, self-heals on reconcile). For a linearizable 'is X deleted?' that must never return a stale-live answer, add an OPT-IN authoritative mode on the per-workspace Durable-Object / CAS lease (the FaaS epic's opt-in path) — optimistic retry / lease live HERE ONLY, never in the default. Build the read-mode selector. Default lock/queue is rejected (reintroduces the per-ws serialization bottleneck the FaaS epic removed).

description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §5.6. Vary M and out-of-range fraction; report rounds/node-fetches/bytes for the surfacing walk vs a naive pull-the-whole-set baseline; show cost tracks match-count not set size; report T_supp overhead (~x2 index nodes; leaves dedup by content).

On green, rewrite the multi-target-deletion Open Question in DESIGN.md (the 'Set-valued verdicts break parallel validation' paragraph) to record the resolution: the 1:N join is a second closure augmentation (T_supp range walk), not a singleton serial pass / full-state scan; suppression stays projection-time so parallel drain + globals-blind rule hold. Log the §6 open sub-questions (death-key domain, envelope exposure, embed-annex placement, GC interaction).

title: OPTIONAL hot-death-key globals cache (subsumed by T_supp head-check)
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3. The future half: a validated death key rides the globals slot (suppress-if set), so incoming facts matching K are suppressed at drain by the existing globals-blind fold — no walk. T_supp closes the past, globals close the future.
notes: SUPERSEDED for correctness by the T_supp head-of-group check, which closes the FUTURE direction too (a future target lands in the K-group; next projection sees the head marker). Keep the globals suppress-if slot ONLY as an optional cache for hot death keys; NOT required for correctness. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.

title: Cloudflare Workers runtime + sizing conformance
description: Run the engine on CF Workers exclusively: R2 store, fold triggered by R2 event notifications to Queues, cold rebuild via a Durable Object alarm loop or copy-the-tree. Conformance: O(log N) mem / O(ms) incremental CPU within 128MB/30s (5min), pile parses in a few MB, Workers-exclusive (no heavy tier).

title: Generational GC (Merkle reachability over a grace window)
description: Reclaim only objects no root within a grace window reaches (git-gc + reflog window). The folder that path-copies stamps superseded nodes with a grace expiry; reclamation lazy, never on the correctness path.

title: Reader modes: fast vs authoritative; RYW/monotonic/causal
description: One read primitive (walk store, pruned by fingerprint, scoped by range). Fast = walk a recent root (may lag). Authoritative = reconcile (root-vs-LIST diff or peer fingerprint diff); empty-prior = full catch-up. RYW client-side (fold own pile after PUT); monotonic reads via a watermark (merge, never replace); causal free from dep-closure.

title: Invalidate generation for direct index commit callers
description: Supported direct/bulk index builders can mutate and commit facts before Node.commit(). Because only merge() normally invalidates the root stamp, a pre-CAS Node.commit failure can leave their ahead index stamped as the old authoritative root across restart. Provide a shared mutation boundary or otherwise invalidate in the same direct mutation transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic direct/bulk builder mutation followed by a pre-CAS failure and restart rebuilds from the old manifest rather than retaining unpublished facts; ordinary bulk seed/benchmark paths remain green.
close_reason: Live merge and supported bulk builders now share commit_index(), which transactionally removes the root stamp; pre-CAS restart regression and all 5k benchmark guards pass.
